records: Now that you're here, you'll have to take me on.
Keep Fernando's cocky challenge without inventing a returning-visitor condition.
A new face! How about a wager? Loser buys a drink. Nothing to it. Just a simple game.
The stake is a drink, not a fee or a cash buy-in.
Here are some coins. We take turns picking up as many as we like, from one to three.
Preserve alternating turns and the one-to-three move limit without inventing a starting count.
Whoever takes the last coin loses. Simple, right? Let's play.
The last-coin taker loses; do not reverse the win condition.
I'll take that drink, then.
Fernando collects the drink after winning the game.
Ahh... That's good. Thanks. See you around.
Retain enjoyment, thanks and the branch's casual farewell.
Tch. You got me. Haven't lost in a while. Here you go.
The alternate result is Fernando losing and paying the stated drink wager.
No, not just now. Tell me, were you really that confident in your gambling?
Hodram declines the drink for now and questions Fernando's confidence.
Sure. Gambling takes two things: insight and luck.
Retain both explicit elements of Fernando's philosophy.
I've got both. You could say I was born to gamble.
This is Fernando's self-confident claim, not an independently established supernatural gift.
You? Insight...?
Preserve Hodram's skepticism as the setup for the demonstration.
Better not judge a man by his looks.
Fernando answers the skeptical assessment with the source's appearance warning.
For instance... That couple over there. Can't hear a word they're saying, but what do you think they're talking about?
Preserve the couple and inability to hear; do not call them married.
He's trying to charm her, I imagine.
Hodram guesses courtship, setting up Fernando's correction.
Come on, this is child's play. They're breaking up.
Fernando predicts separation, not divorce.
Keep Hodram's puzzled pause before the proof.
Just watch.
Fernando invites direct observation of the outcome.
I've heard enough! I just can't understand the way you think anymore. You're so selfish!
The woman condemns her partner's outlook; no marriage or named past offense is added.
Think what you like. I think you're the selfish one.
The man responds with a reciprocal accusation.
Oh, really? Then perhaps we shouldn't see each other anymore.
Preserve the explicit proposal to stop seeing one another.
If that's how we both feel, then we're through.
Keep the breakup as the observed outcome, without inventing legal proceedings.
Hodram silently registers the accurate prediction.
Well? I was right, wasn't I?
Fernando asks Hodram to acknowledge the demonstration.
Impressive... How did you know?
Hodram now asks for the basis rather than disputing the result.
She had her fist clenched under the table. Holding back her anger. That's not how you look when you're talking about love.
Retain the exact visible clue and Fernando's interpretation; do not invent overheard words.
And he never once looked at her. Does that sound like a man sitting across from the woman he loves?
Keep the missing eye contact as the second clue, not a new claim about the couple's history.
I see... You really are remarkably observant.
Hodram concedes Fernando's skill after the evidence.
That's right. With that kind of insight, I can read my opponent's hand.
Connect observation to the stated gambling advantage without adding mind-reading powers.
Add my luck, and I've got the game won.
Preserve Fernando's boast as his own confidence, not a guaranteed game mechanic.
It would be a shame to waste that talent on gambling alone. How about joining my ship?
Hodram recruits for the demonstrated ability rather than promising gambling winnings.
Well, that's a bit sudden.
Fernando reacts to the abrupt employment offer.
Still... I've got time on my hands. I'll toss this coin. Heads, and I'll go with you.
Preserve heads as the joining result and the coin deciding this offer.
Never mind the drink. Join my ship.
Keep the separate repeated recruitment approach rather than another game rule.
That again? ...All right, let's ask the coin one more time.
This variant explicitly repeats the coin decision and must retain that distinction.
Heh. Can't trust my life to someone with your luck. See you around.
The unfavorable coin result leads to refusal; no death or permanent lockout is asserted.
Heh. That settles it. I'll stake my life on you!
The favorable result is an enthusiastic acceptance framed as a wager.
Fernando Dias! That's my name. Call it luck!
Retain the exact corrected Fernando name and the luck motif.
I'll be counting on your skill.
Hodram emphasizes demonstrated ability in response to Fernando's luck boast.
Tch. Slim pickings lately.
The declined-game branch closes with Fernando's disappointed grumble, not an invented fee demand.
This won't do!
Julio's emphatic complaint starts before its target is explained.
Retain Hodram's puzzled reaction.
No, no, no! This simply will NOT do!
Use spoken emphasis for the repeated, drawn-out indignation without an unnatural literal transcript.
(A drunk...)
Keep Hodram's initial private assessment.
Hey! You there!
Julio noisily singles out the party.
Hodram initially remains silent.
Young people these days! Disgraceful!
Preserve the older man's stock complaint without a familial address.
(...The old 'young people these days' routine.)
Hodram recognizes the familiar rant with a dry private aside.
Guzzling this foul excuse for a drink! Disgraceful, the lot of you!
The complaint concerns bad alcohol; no wine, rum or other unbound subtype is supplied.
...(Wonderful.)
Use dry sarcasm for Hodram's dismay, not sincere delight.
What's that sour look for?
Julio challenges Hodram's visible displeasure.
...If you don't like it, you could stop drinking it.
Hodram answers politely but pointedly.
When a man wants a drink, he wants a drink! Beggars can't be choosers.
Localize the necessity idiom to fit the comic drinking excuse; no literal poverty is asserted.
Then perhaps you could drink quietly. Consider the people around you.
Gerhard asks for consideration of the other patrons rather than endorsing the rant.
I may be stuck grumbling over a bad drink, but...
Julio begins explaining what he actually wants.
What I really want is something worth drinking! That's it! You there... Could you get me something good?
Keep the request for good alcohol generic until the inventory condition is separately bound.
Give me a decent drink, and I might quiet down!
Preserve the conditional promise without inventing a recruitment fee.
(Oh, for pity's sake...)
Keep Hodram's weary private response.
Come on, then! My intuition tells me you've got something worth drinking. Don't keep me waiting!
Julio's intuition is his claim, not proof of the party's inventory.
Well, now! You know a thing or two!
The affirmative branch prompts Julio's approval; no particular drink is named.
I'm hardly a connoisseur. I just know what it's worth as a trade good.
Hodram distinguishes basic commercial value from specialist tasting expertise.
Trade, you say! I know a thing or two about trade myself.
Keep Julio's claim of relevant experience without adding a military past.
Did you trade by sea?
Hodram asks about maritime trading experience.
Indeed! You could call me an old hand.
Render べてらん as an experienced seafarer, not a military veteran.
...I see. In that case, may I ask you something?
Hodram asks permission to seek knowledge, not permission to hire Julio yet.
Hm? What would you like to know?
Julio invites the player's chosen kind of question.
An honest willingness to learn. Yes, that's the spirit!
The sincere-question branch wins his approval; distinguish it from testing his ability.
Well, let's be off. Where's your ship?
Julio assumes he will accompany them without an explicit hiring agreement.
Oh, trying to test me, are you? Hmph. I won't have that.
He detects the alternate deliberate test, not an ordinary request for information.
A contrary fellow like you needs a proper education. We'll start with how to recognize a decent drink.
Keep the self-appointed lesson and drink-quality subject without inventing a tasting mechanic.
Well? Don't just stand there! Show me to your ship!
The testing branch also leads to his pushy assumption of passage.
What?
Hodram is surprised by the uninvited boarding plan.
You are taking me aboard, aren't you? I've so much to teach you. A day or two won't be nearly enough!
Preserve the leading assumption and one-or-two-day estimate without an actual prior invitation.
Hodram pauses before Julio introduces himself.
Julio Erneco. Pleased to meet you.
Retain the source-bound Julio Erneco name and its earlier glyph correction.
...Yes. Likewise.
Keep Hodram's hesitant politeness rather than enthusiastic prior consent.
Now see here! The admiral hasn't said a word about letting you aboard...
Gerhard objects and is interrupted; no Grandpa or invented kinship from ご老体.
Oh, let him come.
Hodram finally tolerates the self-invited recruit.
Back to sea at last! Ah, it sets the heart racing!
Keep Julio's excitement at returning after an interval.
Don't lie to me! Don't think you can play dumb just because I'm old. Come on, out with it!
The negative-inventory branch draws Julio's accusation; it is not independent proof that the party has the drink.
No... Well, we were just about to go looking for some. In the course of our voyage, that is.
Hodram's hesitant answer concerns finding good alcohol while sailing, not a new dedicated quest.
A voyage!? Splendid, splendid! Then I'll come along, too.
The alternative route also has Julio invite himself aboard.
Preserve Hodram's startled response to the sudden decision.
Ho ho ho! Why so surprised? I'm a seafaring man, and still going strong!
Retain active seafaring experience, not invented current military service.
Old I may be, but I can still make myself useful!
Julio acknowledges age while asserting practical ability; no precise age is added.
Now see here! The admiral hasn't said a word about letting you aboard...
Retain the separate, identical objection in the alternative recruitment branch.
Oh, let him come.
The same tolerant decision closes the alternative route, as a distinct record.
Julio Erneco. I look forward to sailing with you!
Keep the separate alternative introduction and established spelling.
